Error E-201 means the suction pressure fell below 0.3 bar.

[S1] SOP-MS-003: Oil change on HG-400 gearboxes, SOP-MS-003: Oil change on HG-400 gearboxes
# SOP-MS-003: Oil change on HG-400 gearboxes
This procedure applies the oil change in section 4.3 of the HG-400 manual at Contoso plants and adds the checks that the plants' oil analysis program needs.
1. Lock out the driving motor as SOP-FS-007 describes for pumps; the same steps apply to gearboxes.
2. Take an oil sample from the middle of the sight glass level before draining, and label it with the gearbox tag.
4. Refill with ISO VG 220 oil of the type on the gearbox's lubrication label: 18 liters for an HG-400.
5. Run the gearbox for ten minutes and check the level and the plugs for leaks.
Gearbox GBX-07 on the Lakeside packaging line runs on synthetic PAO oil, so its change interval is 10,000 hours.

[S2] HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual, HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 4 Lubrication › 4.1 Lubrication
The HG-400 is filled at the factory with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 mineral gear oil.
Change the oil after the first 500 operating hours, then every 5,000 operating hours or every 12 months, whichever comes first.
Synthetic PAO oil of the same viscosity extends the interval to 10,000 hours.
Check the oil level weekly at the sight glass with the gearbox stopped.
In operation, the oil temperature must not exceed 90 °C.
## 4.2 Approved oils
Table 4-1 Approved oils
| Oil type | Viscosity grade | Change interval |
|---|---|---|
| Mineral gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
| Synthetic PAO gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 10,000 h or 24 months |
| Food-grade gear oil (NSF H1) | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
When changing from one type to the other, flush the gearbox with the new oil first.

| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Change the oil | As Table 4-1 |

[S1] WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114, WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
# WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
The seal-water line to pump P-201 has a Y-strainer with a 100-micron screen upstream of valve V-114.
A blocked screen is the most common cause of error E-217 at the Riverside plant.
1. Stop P-201 and close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer.
2. Put a bucket under the strainer and release the pressure through the blow-down valve.
3. Unscrew the strainer cap, pull out the screen and rinse it with clean water.
5. Check that the gauge shows a seal-water pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar.

[S2] SOP-FS-007: Pump isolation and lockout, SOP-FS-007: Pump isolation and lockout › Seal-water valves at Riverside
## Seal-water valves at Riverside
At the Riverside plant, the seal-water valve for each pump carries the pump's tag with the prefix V: valve V-114 feeds pump P-201.
Don't close V-114 itself for isolation; close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer, so that V-114's setting is kept.

[S3] Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work, Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
# Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.
Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing.
This bulletin applies to every pump with a mechanical seal flushed by seal water, not only to the CP-200.
At the Riverside plant, report any seal-water line that can't be isolated or drained to the Riverside maintenance planner on extension 4410 before work starts.

[S4] CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual, CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 4 Installation › 4.3 Seal-water connection
## 4.3 Seal-water connection
Connect the seal-water supply to the flush connection marked SW on the seal housing.
The seal-water pressure must exceed the suction pressure by at least 1 bar whenever the pump runs.

Error E-201 means the suction pressure fell below 0.3 bar.
The controller warns for 20 seconds before it trips the pump, to ride through short dips.
Causes, most likely first:

[S1] CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual, CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 7 Maintenance › 7.2 Service intervals
## 7.2 Service intervals
Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings every 2,000 operating hours or six months, whichever comes first.
Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B every 8,000 operating hours.
| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings | 2,000 h or 6 months |
| Regrease the bearings (lithium-complex grease, 15 g per bearing) | 4,000 h |
| Check the coupling alignment | 12 months |
| Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B | 8,000 h |
| Replace the bearings | 32,000 h |
Record every inspection in the maintenance log with the operating hours from the hour meter.
Halve the intervals for pumps that handle abrasive liquids or run above 60 °C.
## 7.3 Lubrication
Regrease each bearing through its grease nipple with the pump running.

[S2] CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual, CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description
# 2 Description
The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C.
The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.
The shaft is sealed by a cartridge mechanical seal flushed with clean seal water from an external supply.
Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft.
A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

[S3] CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual, CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.1 Checks before the first start
# 5 Commissioning
## 5.1 Checks before the first start
1. Check that the rotating assembly turns freely by hand.
2. Check the coupling alignment and fit the coupling guard.
3. Check that the bearings are greased; pumps leave the factory greased for 4,000 hours.
